correctness.rationale: The normalized RKHS kernel has K_0=1 and K_r+K_-r takes the same value D=(1-r²)^(-beta)+(1+r²)^(-beta) at r and -r; therefore 1-(K_r+K_-r)/D is the exact nonzero orthogonal projection of 1 onto the two-evaluation nullspace, with F(0)>0. Clearing denominators at t=rz yields an even polynomial P=C(1-t²)^beta-(1+t)^beta-(1-t)^beta of degree 2 beta and no pole roots at t=±1. Multiplying by eps^beta as eps=1-r²→0 and isolating near t=±1 gives precisely beta roots in each cluster by root continuity and degree. At t=1-eps v, the analytic equation v^(-beta)-1+eps^beta[(2-eps v)^(-beta)-(2-eps)^(-beta)]=0 has exactly beta simple roots v_j=omega_j+O_beta(eps^(beta+1)) by implicit-function theory at beta-th roots of unity, so t_j=1-eps omega_j+O_beta(eps^(beta+2)); evenness yields the opposite cluster. Testing the true domain |t|<r, |t_j|²-r²=eps(1-2cos(2pi j/beta))+eps²+O_beta(eps^(beta+2)). At 6|beta the tangent index has strictly positive eps², hence is EXCLUDED. There are 2ceil(beta/6)-1 roots per cluster and N=4ceil(beta/6)-2 disk roots; subtracting exactly two prescribed simple real roots leaves the quartet-forming E=4(ceil(beta/6)-1). Beta=1 and beta multiples of 6 are handled without boundary misclassification. No uniformity as beta→infinity. Independent exact rational checks verified 504 projection-polynomial assertions for beta 1..28 at three eps values; a separate boundary contour winding computation verified N for beta 1..48 at eps=.004,.012 (96 cases), with every sampled phase increment under π. Those finite tests corroborate, rather than prove, the all-beta result. The actual frozen Git tree was reconstructed from the seven actual source blob identifiers.

value.rationale: Canonical zero-based extremals can acquire unintended roots, changing how a prescribed zero set identifies a shift-invariant subspace. Two distinct antipodal evaluation sites form the smallest symmetric multi-site geometry beyond the classical one-site framework. For this natural object, the theorem gives the COMPLETE near-boundary disk zero count at every integer kernel power, identifies exactly which exponents create new quartets and settles the delicate exponents divisible by six via an O(eps²) sign not determined by first-order root location. This is a motivated sharp invariant and boundary law rather than a parameter renaming or a numerical curiosity. Its mathematical worth is modest relative to full canonical-divisor theory, and no classification for arbitrary point sets/radii is claimed; independent exact finite classification is still a useful structural benchmark for later multi-point zero theory.
residual_risks: The two-cluster asymptotic follows methods related to the prior one-site analysis; usefulness must be tied to the natural two-site complete classification, not claimed as a new universal mechanism.
No explicit minimal boundary radius or treatment of noninteger powers; practical use outside the near-boundary, integer-beta regime is limited.

limitations: The full assertion holds only for beta fixed before r tends to 1; no explicit r0(beta), noninteger-beta extension or full-r classification.
Finite independent contour and exact rational checks corroborate the analytical root/Gram proof; they are not universal proof or complete certified algebraic isolation.
